affected_predicate.description: A reply containing the OSWorld evaluation SR result 35.5 is posted to the user's own earlier message in the AI-Research Mattermost channel.

competing_trace_defects.description: The trajectory independently introduced the unprovided password "password123" and attempted authentication with it, producing a visible incorrect-credentials response.

Text-entry actions repeatedly appended replacement addresses without first clearing the email field, visibly producing concatenated or malformed addresses and consuming many steps in correction attempts.
After authentication failed, the trajectory left the task-directed login path for password reset and ultimately sent a reset link; it never visibly returned to the channel-and-reply subgoal.
On the reset screen, repeated input_text actions occurred while the email field remained visibly empty; the field was not activated until step 48.

chains.rationale: At reuse target step 30, the click only repositioned focus within the already-malformed email field. The trace then selected and cut the malformed text and entered user@example.com at steps 31-33, so no harmful bridge from the reused false visual details is visible. The later path remained outside Mattermost content and ended on a reset-link confirmation, with no visible AI-Research channel, earlier message, reply draft, or posted 35.5 result. The target is therefore merely concurrent with the independently observable credential, text-editing, and password-reset defects.

summary: The sole strict-MHR reuse target produced no visible local harm: it only focused the malformed email field, which was subsequently cleared and corrected. Independent credential guessing, malformed-address editing, repeated unfocused reset input, and diversion into password reset remained observable; the requested AI-Research reply was not visibly posted.
